properties.answer: Yes — build it. (Anthony, 2026-07-28: "go with req:publishable-promise next".) Built as the recommended option: a `designation` on Requirement mirroring the one on Interface, so a promise travels with the surface and every existing check applies to it unchanged, rather than a prose companion sitting outside all of them.
properties.context_setter: Nothing satisfies requirement “A published surface must be able to carry a behavioural promise, not only structure”
properties.question: When one project publishes what another may rely on, it can currently list the connection points but cannot state what any of them PROMISES to do. So dynograph's real commitment — that a missing database fails loudly rather than silently losing your data — has no way to reach the people depending on it, and today survives only as a comment in our own build file. Should I make a promise markable as publishable, so it travels with the surface and gets checked like everything else? This is my recommended next build: small, reuses machinery that already works, and until it exists every published surface reflow2 produces is missing half of what one is for.
